judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow railroad-operations exclusion with a fifty-foot measure and an express sidetrack carve-back; specific and quantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends exclusion (B)(5) of the Broad Form contractual liability text (c135), which is itself garbled in the policy as printed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It recites a statute rather than stating a coverage rule, so what it does to the HPL territory clause is left to inference; the recital is also mis-transcribed in places.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10 (c203) deletes Form 009-118 (10/92) as null and void and substitutes the 2/96 version (c205), yet this text remains in the policy, so two territory amendments coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' is a genuinely uncertain class, and '$1,000,000/$3,000,00C' is mis-typed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It raises professional limits above the declarations' $400,000 each medical incident and the schedule's aggregate (c044), while c187 says an endorsement 'shall not operate to increase the limits of liability as stated in the policy declarations' — a direct limits conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If the need to increase the professional limits ... is ever required' is circular and 'at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' leaves the charge wholly undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with c173's increased limits and with Condition 1 on premium computation (c020), neither of which explains when the option arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Legal or other expenses necessarily incurred by said insured in determining which insurer(s) shall bear the loss' is open-ended, and indemnity is conditioned on the loss ultimately being payable under this policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Other Insurance condition (c027) and the excess clauses (c155, c157, c159), and pulls against Coverage E exclusion (5) (c081), which bars disputes about this insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences establishing a claims-made trigger; clear on their face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The rest of the policy is occurrence-based (c015, c038) and the CGL pollution exclusion is replaced by a total exclusion (c189), so an island of claims-made cover must be reconciled with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The earliest date of any occurrence for which claims ... may be made' mixes occurrence and claims-made concepts in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The retroactive date (3/4/95) precedes the policy period, which must be squared with the 'occurs during the policy period' definitions of bodily injury and property damage (c005, c018).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to the terms of the policy which are not inconsistent herewith' invites argument about which terms survive, and 'attendant clean up costs of property owned by another party' is loosely drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion (c189–c191) bars precisely this liability, including clean-up demands, so the grant and the exclusion point in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard pollutants definition; broad but conventional and closed by its own list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated verbatim in the Total Pollution Exclusion (c192), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No coverage is afforded hereunder for anything which is excluded by the nuclear energy liability exclusion' is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to the nuclear endorsement (c198–c201), which is in fact attached, so the reference holds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deductible, limits and a 'Costs' definition, all with stated figures; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Costs erode limits here whereas Supplementary Payments elsewhere are payable in addition to limits (c002, c169), a structural difference across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'An unlimited extended reporting endorsement will be issued within ninety (90) days' is a mandatory promise, but 'claims which occur during the period of this endorsement or any retroactive date thereof' is garbled and hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the cancellation and non-renewal provisions (c069, c107–c111) which say nothing about this automatic tail obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In an administrative capacity' and 'similar professional boards or committees' after a specific list are both open-textured, and the administrative/clinical line for medical staff is a familiar battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Persons Insured (f) (c058) and with the accreditation-board class (c057), and with the unlicensed-physician endorsement (c037), so the medical-staff insured class is spread across four texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line disapplication of Exclusion (c) for listed functions; its own words are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (c) is also disapplied wholesale by c060, so this narrower disapplication is either redundant or implies the exclusion still bites elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Denying cover for 'the rendering of or failure to render any professional health care services by members of the medical staff' except in student instruction is a sweeping carve-out sitting immediately beside a grant of cover.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with c183's grant, with c058's administrative-duties class and with the charitable-services extension (c090/c196), which covers community care by hospital personnel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short excess-insurance sentence; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is another amendment of the Other Insurance condition (c027), which declares the policy primary, joining c155, c157 and c159.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not operate to increase the limits of liability as stated in the policy declarations' is clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c173 increases professional limits above the declarations and c193 makes limits apply separately by entity, so this no-increase rule and those endorsements cannot all be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amended exclusion is relettered '(a)' although it is exclusion (d), and 'The loading or unloading of patients shall be considered health care services' creates a deeming rule of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 5 (c071) further amends this same form to add air ambulances, and the automobile loading/unloading definition (c168) defines the phrase in property terms, so three texts govern the same words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An instruction identifying the exclusion to be replaced by description rather than by letter, which leaves room for argument about which coverage parts it reaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces CGL exclusion (f) (c121) but says nothing about the Pollution Liability Endorsement (c176–c182), which grants the very cover the replacement removes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, structured absolute pollution exclusion with a hostile-fire carve-back; each limb is specific, though 'pollutants' is famously broad in non-environmental settings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is flatly inconsistent with the Pollution Liability Endorsement's grant of cover for discharges from insured premises (c178) unless one is read as excess or subordinate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean-up-costs exclusion in standard ISO form; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes exactly the 'attendant clean up costs' the Pollution Liability Endorsement insures (c178), a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard pollutants definition; broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the definition in the Pollution Liability Endorsement (c179), so no inconsistency in the term itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the limits apply separately 'with respect to each of the following locations' and then lists three corporate entities, not locations — a mismatch between the operative words and the schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It multiplies the HPL limits set by the declarations and c044, while c187 forbids any increase in declared limits and c173 sets different limits for non-Fund insureds; the three cannot be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is broken into displaced fragments so that the operative sentence ('the coverage ... shall be limited to actual compensatory damages') is severed from its subject, and 'damages does not include the legal fees of any plaintiff' contradicts the earlier reference to legal fees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10 (c203) deletes Form 009-133 as null and void, yet the exclusion remains printed in the policy, so whether it operates at all is a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced provision has its clauses transposed ('when conducted by or on behalf of the named ... insured, the definition of' appears out of place), obscuring the condition on which the redefinition applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It narrows the products hazard definition (c017) only for premises and operations 'described in this endorsement', but no premises or operations are in fact described in it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Charitable health care services in their communities' is undefined and the deeming of such acts as within employment is a strong fiction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Endorsement 9 (c090) verbatim and must be squared with the physician carve-out in c056(d) and the HPL exclusivity clause (c050).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It adds a paragraph (g) defined by reference to 'Section (d) of this endorsement', but this endorsement contains no section (d) — the cross-reference misfires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An identical (g) is already added by c091, and c056(d) excludes Wisconsin-licensed physicians from the employee class it invokes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard ISO nuclear exclusion with defined terms and statutory references; technical but closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is preserved expressly by the Fire Legal Liability clause (c153) and the Pollution Liability Endorsement (c180), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow exclusion for medical payments and first-aid supplementary payments; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Supplementary Payments (c002)(c), which the HPL part also amends (c049), so several texts touch first-aid expense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated nuclear-facility scenarios with a territorial proviso; the paragraph lettering is corrupted in the text but the substance is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of the nuclear endorsement and with the coverages it qualifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitions keyed to the Atomic Energy Act with precise quantities; concrete throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands 'property damage' to include radioactive contamination, an express override of c018 confined to this endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deletes two forms by number; clear in form, but it is dated 6/21/1996 while stating it is effective on the inception date, which affects claims arising in between.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deleted forms — the Trebled Damages Exclusion (c194) and the 10/92 territory endorsement (c172) — remain physically in the policy, so the instrument contains provisions declared null and void.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line attachment of a replacement form; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The substituted form (c205) is in fact attached, so the reference holds, though the schedule of endorsements still lists the deleted 10/92 version.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It recites a statute rather than stating a coverage rule, and the heading cites s.655.27(5)(a)2 while the quoted text is headed s.655.27(5), a mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces c172 (deleted by c203) and amends the HPL territory clause (c045), whose own territorial words are missing, so the effective territory must be assembled from three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple address correction for a scheduled location; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It changes the CGL schedule of locations, which also defines 'insured premises' (c149), but the change is express and dated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a location with class code and premium basis; concrete data entry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands 'insured premises' (c149) mid-term while stating it is effective on inception, a small timing wrinkle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-name addition to the named insured schedule; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Form 009-052 (c092), whose bar on automatic coverage for newly acquired entities already sits against c163.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It attaches 'Form 008-145' without describing what that form does, so the provision's content cannot be determined from its own words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No form numbered 008-145 appears in the schedule of endorsements or in the policy as produced, so the instrument refers to a term it does not contain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An add/delete schedule amendment with an address and square footage; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says it is effective on the inception date although dated 11/21/1996, and it deletes a location (200 W. Silver Spring) that is not obviously the one scheduled, which bears on 'insured premises' (c149).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single deletion from a scheduled list; clear, although it is dated after the policy period expired while purporting to be effective at inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address deleted (1000 North 92nd St., Wauwatosa) does not match the scheduled entry (1000 N. 92nd St., Milwaukee) in Form L9259a, so the amendment and the schedule do not line up.
